note: A kind of reader, not a person. Every name, date and line here is fictional; nobody has been sent this page. The personal part (a reader's name) would travel only in the link's fragment, which the browser never sends.
title: For a security leader
reader: a CISO or security leader at a large company
judges: Can I take this to my board; does it map to policy, audit and accountability; would I trust this team?
why_you: You carry the risk this book is about. If the controls in these chapters would not survive your audit committee, we would rather hear it from you now than from a reader later.

ask.by_note: an example date: nothing has been sent

gets: your name in the acknowledgements, if you want it there
the first edition when it ships
a reply to every comment, and a page showing what your comments changed

chapters.why: the controls, as policy you can read
accountability: who signs, and what a signature holds
the argument: the team as the insider, and which controls it leaned on

questions.q: In one sentence, what does this chapter ask a security leader to believe?
Where did you need a term or a step explained that the page did not give you?
Which of these controls would you call a control in your own policy, and which only an intention?
What could you put in place next week, and what would need budget or a board decision?
Who, in this chapter, is accountable for what an agent does? Is that clear to you?
Does "a signature" here mean what it would mean in your firm? Where does it differ?
Would this way of deciding survive an auditor's question? Which question would break it?
What would you have to add before you let a team work this way?
Does the chapter convince you that a well-behaved team of agents is still an insider risk? Why, or why not?
Which control here would you trust, and which depends on the agents choosing to follow it?
What risk did you expect to see that the chapter does not name?
Is anything here described in a way that would help someone get round a control? Mark it.
What would you tell your board after reading this chapter?

short_note: the one chapter to read when short of time: a proposal by developer@ from synthetic@'s runs, for the editor to keep or change
